findings.evidence: scripts/check-hot-path-bench.sh calls finish immediately after the unknown-marker loop (line ~136), again after the stale-NOT_YET_BUILT loop (line ~161), before ever reaching the uncovered-required-row loop. scripts/lib.sh's fail() docstring: 'Records the failure; the caller keeps going so one run reports every violation rather than only the first.' Reproduced: a fixture with both an unknown hot-path marker and a NOT_YET_BUILT entry that has become stale (a real marker now covers it) reports only the unknown-marker FAIL line; removing the unknown marker then reveals the stale-entry FAIL in a second run. Contrast with scripts/check-requirements-trace.sh, scripts/check-file-size.sh, scripts/check-readmes.sh and scripts/check-portability.sh, all added in this same checkpoint's commits, which accumulate every problem before a single terminal report.
findings.summary: check-hot-path-bench.sh reports only the first of its three failure categories per run (an early `finish` after each), unlike every sibling gate added this checkpoint and unlike lib.sh's own documented fail() contract that one run should report every violation.
